messages:
alex: quick thread — I put together an interop playbook draft for Dedicated customers migrating from Spot/elastic into Reserved pools. want feedback on launch criteria, monitoring hooks, and quota translation rules.

maria: nice, can you drop the checklist here so we can iterate?

alex: pasted initial checklist snippet below. high level only for now:
```
- preflight: quota mapping complete (tenant -> pool)
- config: spillover disabled by default, region affinity enforced
- canary: 5% traffic, 1-hour ramp, verify p95/p99 & error rate thresholds
- observability: per-pool latency, KV cache hit, burst_consumption, cost per-token
- billing: daily export with burst accounting columns
- rollback: automated traffic drain + route fallback to hosted non-reserved pool
- acceptance tests: perf with seq_len=1024, concurrency=50, both quantized and fp16
```

jonathan: couple Qs — what's the canonical translation rule from existing "burst credits" to Reserved "burst units"? need formula for billing and headroom.

priya: suggestion: measure burst in GPU-ms or token-ms then translate via a per-model conversion factor. metric names we should emit: `reserved.pool.burst_ms`, `reserved.pool.kvcache_hit_rate`, `reserved.pool.p95_latency`.

sam: from billing side we need: pool_id, tenant_id, burst_used_tokens, burst_used_ms, start_ts, end_ts, model_variant. CSV schema please.

ops-bot: CI: playbook linter passed for ci/playbooks/dedicated-interop. Tests: smoke-run, canary-sim.

elaine: launch gating note — add explicit SLA acceptance checklist: target p95 latency <= customer_sla_p95 + 10%, error_rate < 0.5% during canary. Also require a documented fallback contact list.

maria: also: region affinity rules are a common ask. customers who are regulated want cross-region spillover off by default and an explicit opt-in.

alex: agreed. adding config sample to repo:
```yaml
reserved_pools:
  spillover:
    enabled: false
    max_cross_region: 0
  region_affinity: REQUIRED
  canary_config:
    percent: 5
    duration: 1h
```

jonathan: autoscale policy Q — what cooldown windows do we want? scale-out short, scale-in longer. propose scale_out_cooldown=120s, scale_in_cooldown=300s. also want smoothing to avoid oscillation during traffic spikes.

priya: agreed on cooldowns. acceptance tests should include a spike test (2x traffic for 2 minutes) and observe no more than 1 scale action per 2m. also run bench with seq_len=1024 and quantized paths (8-bit) to validate perf delta.

sam: legal/compliance note: for enterprise customers with contracts we need to retain routing and audit logs for 180 days. will the playbook call that out?

alex: yes — adding a retention section and audit hooks.

maria: bottleneck question — if we disable spillover, we need explicit runbook for capacity shortfall: notify customer, auto-throttle non-critical traffic, enable surge-buy if approved. add escalation path.

ops-bot: runbook template created: ci/runbooks/dedicated_capacity_shortfall.md (draft).

elaine: also add an observability dashboard template: per-tenant tokens/sec, burst burn rate, pool headroom %. that made debugging much faster during the early pilot.

jonathan: can someone own the conversion factor matrix by model? I can help map for our top 5 models.

priya: i'll add the alert rules to the repo (pager thresholds, slack channels, runbooks).

sam: i'll prototype the billing export by EOD and ping finance for approval on the CSV schema.

alex: thanks all. I'll update the doc and open a PR: target to onboard the ACME pilot next week. Any immediate blockers?

maria: finance approval on committed capacity is the main blocker. pinging @finance in a sec.

jonathan: i'm good to help on the canary dashboard and metrics wiring.

priya: i'll finish the alerting playbook and the acceptance test harness.

sam: will confirm billing export and legal retention constraints.

alex: awesome — will post PR link when ready. appreciate the quick turnaround :rocket:
